skill.name: control-loop-extraction
skill.description: Analyze AI agent frameworks by locating reasoning loops, step functions, and termination conditions, then documenting how each loop executes and stops.
skill.summary: Documents how agent frameworks reason, dispatch actions, and terminate execution loops.
skill.author: Dowwie

security_audit.summary: All static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline examples in SKILL.md. The skill contains documentation for analyzing agent loops, with no executable scripts, network access, shell commands, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent found.

static_findings.snippet: | Step limit | `if step_count >= max_steps` | May cut off valid execution |
| Token limit | `if total_tokens >= max_tokens` | May truncate mid-thought |
| Explicit finish | `if action.type == "finish"` | Relies on LLM cooperation |
| Loop detection | `if state in seen_states` | Requires state hashing |
| Error threshold | `if error_count >= max_errors` | May exit on recoverable errors |
| Step limit | `if step_count >= max_steps` | May cut off valid execution |

content.value_statement: Agent frameworks hide reasoning loops across scattered files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to find loops, step functions, and termination conditions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, Reflection, and Tree-of-Thoughts patterns.
Guides users to locate the main agent execution loop.
Breaks down step functions into input assembly, model call, parsing, and dispatch.
Catalogs termination conditions such as step limits, token limits, timeouts, and loop detection.
Provides a structured report template for documenting loop behavior.
limitations: Requires source code access to the agent framework under review.
Does not execute automated static analysis or build a dependency graph.
May need another mapping skill to find relevant files in large repositories.
Does not prove runtime behavior without tests or traces.

use_cases.title: Review an Agent Framework
use_cases.description: Map the main loop, step function, and stop conditions before making architecture changes.

use_cases.title: Document Execution Flow
use_cases.description: Create a clear control loop report for maintainers and reviewers.

use_cases.title: Compare Reasoning Patterns
use_cases.description: Classify how different frameworks plan, act, reflect, and terminate.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Main Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a known agent repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use control-loop-extraction on this repository. Find the main agent loop and summarize its purpose, file location, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Extract the Step Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review after likely agent files are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these agent files with control-loop-extraction. Break the step function into input assembly, model call, parsing, dispatch, and result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Reasoning Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare implementation against known agent patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use control-loop-extraction to classify this framework as ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, Reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts, hybrid, or other. Explain the evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Termination Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for reliability and runaway loop risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply control-loop-extraction to audit all termination paths. Identify missing guards, weak loop detection, retry limits, timeout behavior, and recovery paths.

output_examples.input: A repository with an agent runner and tool dispatch module.
output: Reasoning pattern: ReAct with a Thought, Action, Observation cycle.
Step function: builds messages, calls the model, parses tool requests, and dispatches tools.
Termination: final answer, step limit, tool error threshold, and timeout.

output_examples.input: A framework that plans tasks before executing them.
output: Reasoning pattern: Plan-and-Solve with conditional replanning.
Loop location: planner runner and executor coordination files.
Risk note: replanning needs a bounded retry limit and clear failure state.

best_practices: Start with repository mapping so likely agent files are in scope.
Cite file locations for every loop, step function, and termination condition.
Separate observed behavior from inferred design intent.
anti_patterns: Do not classify a framework from naming alone.
Do not ignore retry, timeout, and error threshold paths.
Do not treat sample code as proof of runtime behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes how an AI agent loop reasons, calls models, dispatches actions, and stops.

faq.question: Does it run code?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill that guides source review and report creation.

faq.question: Which reasoning patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, Reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts, and hybrid designs.

faq.question: Can it find every agent file automatically?
faq.answer: No. It may need repository mapping first, especially in large or unfamiliar codebases.

faq.question: What should the final output include?
faq.answer: The output should include topology, step function details, termination conditions, and loop detection notes.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Engineers, researchers, and technical writers can use it to understand agent framework behavior.
